summary: Adversarially test whether the OpenVLA silent-vision-bypass finding is actually novel

evidence.finding: openvla/openvla issues (all states, gh api + gh search, keywords: constant action, same action, identical output, ignores image, vision not used, blind, transformers version, DynamicCache, past_key_values, prepare_inputs_for_generation, cache, generate, prompt truncation, 4.40, 4.50): zero issues describe this exact mechanism. Closest are #62 'Issue with Repeating Model Output After Fine-Tuning' (closed 2024-08-22, symptom matches 'identical action' but maintainers attributed it to bad/duplicated training data or action-chunking, never diagnosed a transformers-version cache bug) and #148 'Cached Generation vs Multimodal Forward' (closed 2024-11-01 with zero replies) which points at the exact code region — the reporter noticed that the cached-generation forward call does not pass multimodal_embeddings — but frames it as a design question, not a version-triggered failure, and gets no answer. #266 and #313 are generic transformers-version/forward-vs-generate questions with no bug diagnosis.
evidence.source: gh api repos/openvla/openvla/issues (state=all) and gh search issues --repo openvla/openvla, issues #62, #148, #266, #313

evidence.finding: HuggingFace openvla/openvla-7b has 7 discussion threads total (none about this), plus the 4 LIBERO-finetuned repos each have exactly 1 discussion (all just model-card edits, one unrelated to a 'GoBA' backdoor-attack paper). PR discussion #5 on openvla-7b ('Update modeling_prismatic.py to account for the case where input_ids is None') touches the same forward()/generation code but fixes a different edge case (missing input_ids null-check), not the Cache-vs-None issue, and remains open/unmerged.

The vulnerable line `if past_key_values is not None: input_ids = input_ids[:, -1:]` in prepare_inputs_for_generation, and the matching `if input_ids.shape[1] == 1 and past_key_values is not None` branch in forward(), is copy-pasted verbatim, unpatched, across every fork/derivative found via GitHub code search (TRI-ML/prismatic-vlms — the upstream base — OpenDriveLab/RoboDual, PKU-HMI-Lab/Hybrid-VLA, umd-huang-lab/tracevla, and ~25 others). No fork rewrites this check for Cache-object semantics (e.g. via get_seq_length()), i.e. nobody has silently fixed it either.
evidence.source: gh api search/code?q=prepare_inputs_for_generation+prismatic and per-repo greps of prismatic.py in TRI-ML/prismatic-vlms, OpenDriveLab/RoboDual, PKU-HMI-Lab/Hybrid-VLA, umd-huang-lab/tracevla

evidence.finding: moojink/openvla-oft — the dominant successor fork — never calls .generate() for action prediction at all. Its predict_action() always does a single forward pass with past_key_values=None explicitly (parallel/regression or diffusion decoding), so it structurally never enters the autoregressive cached-generation code path the claim is about. This is an unrelated architectural choice (throughput), not a diagnosed fix for this bug; it also pins its own transformers fork (moojink/transformers-openvla-oft, forked for bidirectional attention) rather than stock transformers.

Direct inspection of transformers generation/utils.py across v4.40.1, v4.41.0, v4.44.0, v4.46.0, v4.48.0, v4.50.0 and current main shows the claimed mechanism does not fire for OpenVLA. `_prepare_cache_for_generation()` only writes an empty `DynamicCache()` into model_kwargs before step 0 if `self._supports_default_dynamic_cache()` is True, which requires the class attribute `_supports_cache_class = True`. OpenVLA's PrismaticPreTrainedModel/PrismaticForConditionalGeneration/OpenVLAForActionPrediction never set this attribute, so they inherit PreTrainedModel's default `_supports_cache_class = False` and hit 'Quick escape route 3' (`if not self._supports_default_dynamic_cache(): return`), which has existed continuously since at least v4.41-4.44. Net effect: on the very first prepare_inputs_for_generation call, past_key_values is simply absent from model_kwargs, so the function parameter falls back to its declared default of None -- exactly the pre-4.36 behavior -- and the multimodal branch (which consumes pixel_values) runs normally.

Separately, from v4.50 onward PreTrainedModel stops inheriting GenerationMixin, which would ordinarily make .generate() disappear entirely for OpenVLA's classes (they only inherit PreTrainedModel, not GenerationMixin) -- a loud AttributeError, not a silent bug. But transformers explicitly guards against this for trust_remote_code models loaded via an Auto class (exactly how OpenVLA's own README loads it, via AutoModelForVision2Seq.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)): dynamic_module_utils.py's add_generation_mixin_to_remote_model() detects a custom class with prepare_inputs_for_generation but no explicit GenerationMixin base and dynamically re-injects it, preserving .generate() with the same _supports_cache_class=False behavior described above.
evidence.source: raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/transformers/main/src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py (add_generation_mixin_to_remote_model) and modeling_utils.py (can_generate warning text naming v4.50)

evidence.finding: openvla/openvla pins transformers==4.40.1 in setup.py, pyproject.toml and requirements-min.txt -- the officially supported version, well below the range the claim describes -- so a user following the repo's own install instructions is never exposed to whatever residual risk exists on later versions.

checks.closest_prior_art: github.com/openvla/openvla issue #148 'Cached Generation vs Multimodal Forward' (closed 2024-11-01, https://github.com/openvla/openvla/issues/148) is the closest match -- it identifies the exact code region (the cached-generation forward() branch that skips multimodal_embeddings) that the claim's mechanism hinges on, but frames it as a design question about why that branch exists at all, gets zero replies, and never connects it to a transformers-version/Cache-object regression. Issue #62 'Issue with Repeating Model Output After Fine-Tuning' (closed 2024-08-22) is the closest phenomenological match to the claimed symptom (constant/identical actions) but was attributed to training-data or action-chunking causes, not this mechanism. No issue, PR, HF discussion, or fork anywhere diagnoses 'transformers>=4.50 silently truncates the prompt via an empty DynamicCache.'
checks.honest_assessment: Two separate questions, and they point the same way. (1) Has anyone already reported this exact bug? No -- exhaustive search of every openvla/openvla issue and PR (all states), every HF discussion on openvla-7b and its four LIBERO-finetuned checkpoints, ~30 GitHub forks' modeling_prismatic.py files, HN, and arXiv turns up nothing that names this mechanism. (2) Is the mechanism actually correct? Based on directly reading transformers' generation/utils.py and dynamic_module_utils.py across seven versions (4.40.1 through current main), the answer appears to be no. Transformers has an explicit, purpose-built escape hatch (`_supports_cache_class`, checked in `_prepare_cache_for_generation`'s 'Quick escape route 3') that has existed continuously since the Cache-class migration began (~v4.41-4.44) specifically so that legacy/custom models which never opted into the new Cache API keep getting `past_key_values=None` on their first generate() call, not an empty DynamicCache. OpenVLA's custom code never sets `_supports_cache_class = True`, so it rides this escape hatch on every version I checked, including 4.50.0 and main. Separately, the v4.50 removal of GenerationMixin from PreTrainedModel -- which would otherwise break .generate() outright for OpenVLA with a loud AttributeError -- is also explicitly guarded for exactly this trust_remote_code+Auto-class scenario via `add_generation_mixin_to_remote_model`. So the claim isn't just unreported, it looks like a plausible-sounding but incorrect diagnosis: it describes a real, well-known class of transformers migration hazard (custom/trust_remote_code models and the Cache-object transition -- this part is extensively documented in transformers' own code comments and deprecation warnings) but attaches it to a specific instance and code path that transformers was deliberately hardened against years before v4.50. An expert who traced the actual generation/utils.py logic would say 'no, that specific failure mode doesn't fire here, and here's the exact guard clause that prevents it' rather than being impressed. I could not run the actual model (no GPU/torch in this sandbox) to empirically confirm end-to-end, so I can't rule out some other version, attention backend, or serving-wrapper interaction producing a related-but-different silent failure -- but the specific causal chain in the claim (empty DynamicCache at step 0 -> prepare_inputs_for_generation truncates to 1 token -> forward() takes the cached-generation branch -> pixel_values never consumed) is directly contradicted by the guard clause that gates exactly that DynamicCache initialization on an attribute OpenVLA's classes never set.

checks.scope: OpenVLA quantization / modern-stack claims only (unrelated checks from the same audit run were removed before publishing)

evidence.finding: The original authors already quantized OpenVLA-7B to int8 and int4 and reported memory + real-robot-rollout success rate: bf16=16.8GB/71.3% success, int8=10.2GB/58.1%, int4=7.0GB/71.9% success (80 rollouts, 8 BridgeData V2 tasks). This is a more rigorous version of Project A's 'quantize to 4-bit and measure damage' claim, done in 2024 by the model's own creators using physical robot outcomes rather than cosine similarity.

evidence.source: github.com/moojink/openvla-oft issue #108 (closed 2025-08-21), filed by the OpenVLA paper's own first author's fork
evidence.finding: Documents the exact fix for the _supports_sdpa incompatibility: '_supports_sdpa = False should be added' in modeling_prismatic.py for transformers 4.55.1 / peft 0.17.0 — the identical root cause and identical one-line fix Project A claims to have found independently, published roughly a year prior by someone directly downstream of the original authors.

An existing, more sophisticated public study of OpenVLA quantization damage: GPTQ+BiLLM Hessian-guided 1-bit/4-bit mixed quantization, reporting gripper-specific L1 error and cosine similarity across multiple calibration strategies (e.g. cosine 0.825-1.000, gripper L1 0.118-0.552 depending on calibration set). This directly overlaps and exceeds Project A's single nf4 cosine-0.743/2-of-16-flips data point, and predates it by weeks.

evidence.source: github.com/pytorch/ao issue #3236 (2025-10-24) and openvla/openvla issues #286, #287 (2025-12 to 2026-02)
evidence.finding: Multiple independent parties were already quantizing OpenVLA-7B to 4-bit and hitting/reporting bugs (bitsandbytes .to() errors, torchao GemliteUIntX slowdowns) well before this session — confirms 4-bit OpenVLA is a well-trodden, actively-worked path, not a novel target.

Tenstorrent already ships a reference CPU (device='cpu') PyTorch benchmark script for OpenVLA as part of their hardware-porting effort, i.e. CPU-only OpenVLA inference and benchmarking already exists elsewhere as a reference point.

evidence.source: github.com/huggingface/transformers issues #41622, #39974; and issues on kijai/ComfyUI-Florence2, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR, XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Audio, etc.
evidence.finding: '_supports_sdpa missing' and 'GenerationMixin not inherited / ImportError' are an extremely common, well-documented bug class across dozens of custom-remote-code HF multimodal models whenever transformers ships a breaking release — the general failure pattern and fix (add the attribute / explicitly inherit GenerationMixin) is thoroughly known; applying it to OpenVLA specifically is a mechanical reapplication, not a new technique.

evidence.source: GitHub code/issue search for 'silent vision bypass' / cache_position slicing bug specific to OpenVLA modeling_prismatic.py
evidence.finding: Could not find a prior report of the exact 'empty-cache prompt slicing silently drops vision tokens' bug for OpenVLA specifically — this narrow instance appears to not have a public prior report, though it is a specific case of the broader well-known 'custom multimodal generate()/cache handling silently breaks across transformers versions' bug family seen on many other VLMs.

Confirms the 'edge-VLA inference runtime' space is actively occupied right now by other real, current projects (vla.cpp = general VLA inference runtime; FlashRT = production low-latency VLA control for Pi0/Pi0.5/GR00T-N1.6/Pi0-FAST). Neither targets OpenVLA's specific transformers-compat shims, so they don't directly refute that one narrow piece, but they do show the broader goal ('make VLA inference lean and deployable') is a crowded, live field, not a gap Project A discovered.
